children: Stocks are under pressure ahead of a big day for Nvidia, with the chip maker's interim CEO set to address Wall Street after last week's dramatic ouster of co-founder Jensen Huang.

Nvidia is expected to report another quarter of strong revenue growth, but investors will be watching Colette Kress's call with analysts for guidance on the company's future. The interim chief is expected to rein in Nvidia's aggressive dealmaking, a practice that has been backstopping the broader AI economy.
Huang meanwhile put out a statement today saying he is willing to return to Nvidia as chief executive should he be asked by directors to do so.

The fallout from Huang's Chinese spying scandal continues to ripple around the world. Chip stocks slid in Asia today, after the Commerce Department issued a long-awaited rule to crack down on shipments of chips from Nvidia and other U.S. companies to China.
Back in the U.S., Nvidia shares are continuing their decline. All three major indexes are in the red by 1% or more.
This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
